Updated view incorporating SLOOS: The FOMC statement remains cautious about the recovery and committed to highly accommodative policy. SLOOS evidence softens that caution somewhat. Large banks eased standards for several mortgage categories (GSE-eligible, QM jumbos, and QM non-jumbo, non-GSE-eligible), suggesting improving household credit availability. Foreign banks reported strengthened demand for C&I loans, and some small banks expect stronger demand for consumer loans. Still, banks frequently cite the economic outlook, industry-specific problems, and lower risk tolerance as reasons for tighter standards, indicating lingering headwinds, especially for business credit. Net tone: cautious but showing early signs of easing credit conditions and firmer demand versus the earlier, more negative read.
